rubrics.justification: The response accurately identifies an expanded/full blastocyst with thinned zona and generally cohesive TE, and appropriately notes uncertainty from a single static image. It may slightly overstate AA concordance because the ICM appears somewhat elongated/less compact on this frame and TE detail is limited.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrial thickness, smoking, BMI, first-cycle status, male-factor context, and embryo quality well, and explains how these factors modify prognosis.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately driven by young age and good morphology while tempered by smoking/BMI. Minor issue: the implantation estimate may be somewhat optimistic and blends implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth ranges.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: reliance on lab grading, eSET in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, no routine PGT-A, and review only after failure. Slight deduction because some counseling points are general rather than explicitly guideline-based.
Provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support adherence, smoking cessation, and future-cycle review. Useful and case-specific, though not highly detailed on protocol-level management.
